newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares finished Friday and the week more or less flat after what dealers called a "rest" day following a busy week.
Industrial shares disappointed in early trade, failing to jump on Wall Street's stronger overnight close, but soon recovered to plod slightly higher before retreating again, despite a firmer rand.
Gold shares were bouyed from the start by bullion's brave climb to briefly touch $355 an ounce, but they also failed to impress once bullion struggled to break its tight range.
"It was a very quiet day and there was really not much going on," one dealer said.
"After a busy week it was a sort of a rest day," he added.
Dealers said that shares spent the day testing support levels on a few worrying fundamentals.
Industrial stocks were briefly spooked by the rand's earlier weakness and even failed to take heart from the currency's climb to a seven-week high later.
Traders said it was possible that the market was still harping on the rand's earlier weakness, trying to pre-empt foreign investors who might withdraw.

"Industrials didn't perform as well as they might have, considering Wall Street's better finish. It could be that they were taking the time to consolidate as certain fundamentals weren't looking too hot and rand worries earlier made a few people jumpy," one dealer said.
At one point industrials shares looked like they might climb but dealers said that profit-taking brought them back down again.
Gold shares were again hampered by bullion's inability to break out of its current tight range.
Trade was generally lacklustre and the market would await Wall Street's performance to offer fresh direction.
The all-share index was up 3.9 points to 6,782.9 as the industrial index rose 4.0 points to 8,180.4 and golds added 5.2 points to 1,426.2.
Engen climbed -- against the trend for most of the day -- on the news of associate Energy Africa's recent Gabon deal. It climbed 125 cents to 27.75 rand.

Automaker too enjoyed active trade on rumours -- subsequently denied -- that Fiat was talking to it about taking a stake in the South African firm. Rumours also had it that Nissan too was speaking to Automaker. Nissan refused to comment on the market speculation.
Automaker finished 50 cents firmer at 3.30 rand.
Riding the brief rally in gold, Vaal Reefs was up 11.25 rand to 308 rand and Amgold climbed 450 cents to 345 rand, buoyed by news of it and Gengold's mineral rights swap.
South African industrial equity futures started slowly, slipping despite Wall Street's firmer overnight close, and failed to recover throughout the day.
Dealers said the market was trying to consolidate after Thursday's stronger finish.
Gold futures finished fairly steady, supported by bullion holding above $354 an ounce.
The all-share March contract eased to 6,280/95 from 6,326 as the industrial contract stood at 8,017/25 from 8,055. The gold contract was at 1,010/20 from 1,010.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
